q: How much N2O does an adipic acid plant emit?
title: Adipic acid plant N2O emissions
short: Adipic acid is made by oxidising a cyclohexanone and cyclohexanol mix with nitric acid, which releases nitrous oxide. The IPCC 2006 default is 300 kg N2O per tonne without abatement, about 82 tonnes CO2e at a GWP of 273. Abatement units destroy most of it.
audience: Chemical plant managers and buyers of nylon 6,6 intermediates

p: The nitric acid oxidation step forms nitrous oxide, which leaves with the off-gas. Without abatement it is by far the largest emission source, much larger than fuel.

ul: Tonnes of adipic acid produced each month.
N2O measured in the off-gas, or the abatement unit's destruction rate and running hours.
Fuel and electricity for the plant, as Scope 1 and 2 CO2.

p: N2O is Scope 1. Convert it with the AR6 100-year GWP of 273 and state the hours the abatement unit was off, since a few days of bypass can outweigh a month of normal running.

example.title: Worked example (illustrative figures)
lines: With 90 percent destruction: 300 tonnes N2O remain.

senseible: Senseible reads bills, fuel invoices and production records into dated, fingerprinted records, so the figure you send a buyer can be traced to its documents.
